blocks.heading: Drawing the life-cycle model
blocks.text: Put time on the horizontal axis and sales on the vertical axis. Draw low introductory sales, a rising growth section, a high flatter maturity section and a declining section. Label the stages so the reader can distinguish the changes in the sales pattern. Some descriptions distinguish saturation within the mature plateau. The curve is conceptual unless data are supplied; do not present it as actual measured sales or assume a given number of years per stage. Extension actions such as adapting the product or finding new buyers can sometimes prolong sales but do not guarantee revival.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text:
Construct an illustrative life cycle for a lunch-container range, with no numerical sales data provided. ![Product life cycle](diagrams/product-life-cycle.png)

The labelled diagram shows the model’s changing sales direction rather than forecasts for a real range. Maturity does not mean zero sales, and decline is falling sales rather than necessarily an immediate end to all demand.
